## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṇṇakajātaka* (Ja 401), also referred to as the *Dasaṇṇaka Jātaka*, is a birth story in the canonical Pali Jātaka collection [Boriharnwanaket]. The narrative opening (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha addresses a monk tempted to backslide due to desire for his former wife. The Buddha remarks that she had caused him harm in a previous life as well, when he nearly died of heartsickness on her account and was saved through the counsel of wise men. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta is identified as the wise royal councillor Senaka, alongside Sāriputta as the wise Pukkusa and Mahā-Moggallāna as the wise Āyura; the tale is expounded in the commentary to illustrate the dangers and disadvantages of clinging, stemming from the infatuation of the king's household priest's son with the queen [Boriharnwanaket].
